title: Every Prime Agent governance action must be enacted as an edit to its Agent Artifact
content:
A.1.14.2.6.1 states the rule in one line: "All governance actions taken by a Prime Agent must be enacted through edits to their Agent Artifact." There is no channel by which an Agent can govern outside its text — the Artifact is not documentation of decisions, it *is* the decision record and the current state.

A.1.14.2.7 fixes the routes: "There are two mechanisms for Agents to edit their respective Agent Artifacts: Root Edits and Omni Documents." Under A.1.14.2.7.1, the Root Edit process "enables Prime Agent token holders to hold a vote on a proposed Artifact update. If that vote is successful, the Prime Agent's designated Executor Agent will modify the Prime Agent Artifact as directed." Under A.1.14.2.7.2, Omni Documents encode operational or business logic spanning multiple Primitives or covering inherited non-Primitive infrastructure, and may either mirror Sky Primitive schemas or use custom ones.

The combination gives a clean two-speed model. Novel decisions require a token holder vote; recurring decisions are pre-authorized once as Omni logic and then executed repeatedly without a vote — the same amortization pattern the Linear Interpolation Module applies to protocol parameters.

The deeper consequence is auditability. Because nothing counts as governance unless it appears as an Artifact edit, the Artifact's history is a complete log of the Agent's governance, and any action without a corresponding edit is by construction unauthorized. That is what makes the maintenance obligation in A.1.14.2.10.1 — that the Artifact "provides clear authorization for all actions taken by the Agent" — enforceable rather than aspirational.
description: There are exactly two edit mechanisms — a Root Edit token holder vote implemented by the Executor Agent, or deterministic logic already encoded in an Omni Document.
